title: Add Token Fidelity Index and adaptive alert quieting for noisy token-cost signals
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our token-level cost and latency signals produce frequent low-value alerts during high-variance workloads (chatty clients, large token bursts, synthetic traffic). Pager noise reduces trust in SLO alerts and slows incident response. This PR introduces the Token Fidelity Index (TFI): a per-invocation score representing how well a traced invocation's token-level measurements reflect stable production behavior. TFI is used to drive an adaptive alert quieting controller that suppresses or demotes alerts when the metric signal is dominated by low-fidelity invocations.

What this PR does (summary): adds TFI calculation and export, enriches OpenTelemetry spans with TFI tags, implements a Prometheus rule + alert manager muting strategy that uses TFI rollups, and ships a dashboard + runbook updates for operators. Includes unit and integration tests and an end-to-end synthetic replay bench to validate quieting behavior.

Key goals: reduce alert churn from token-cost/latency tail noise by at least 40% in noisy windows, while preserving true positive SLO breaches. Provide operators diagnostic panels to see fidelity distribution and unmuted alert candidates.

Implementation notes: - Token Fidelity Index (tfi_score): computed at the ingestion layer using a lightweight two-factor heuristic: (1) shape-matching of prompt/response token-length distribution against historical cohort, and (2) burst-normalized token-latency variance. Score is 0.0-1.0; higher is better fidelity. - Metrics: new prometheus metrics redwood_tfi_score{tenant,route,model} (histogram + gauge), redwood_tfi_rollup_unmuted_count and redwood_tfi_rollup_muted_count. - Tracing: spans get attribute telemetry.tfi_score and telemetry.tfi_reason for fast triage. - Alerting: new recording rules compute per-tenant TFI quantiles and a muting controller consults these signals to demote alerts with median TFI < 0.25 for synthetic-heavy windows. The controller is conservative: it first mutes low-priority cost alerts, then escalates to more aggressive thresholds only after operator opt-in. - Dashboard: tfi_overview.jsonnet adds a fidelity distribution panel, an unmuted-alert candidates view, and a historical fidelity vs false-positive chart. - Runbook: added runbooks/alerts/tfi_quieting.md describing rationale, opt-in, and rollback steps.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for score logic and span enrichment. - Integration test that replays synthetic and production-shaped traffic to confirm alert reduction and retention of real SLO breaches. - Canary rollout plan: start on dedicated-canary region for two weeks, evaluate alert churn and missed-alert rates, then gradual rollout with 10% steps.

Checklist: - [x] Add TFI computation and unit tests - [x] Export Prometheus metrics and recording rules - [x] Enrich OTEL spans and update span schema docs - [x] Add dashboard panels and runbook - [x] Integration test and replay harness - [x] Safety gate: opt-in via config flag per-tenant

Related work items: Linear ENG-2345 (observability noise project) and ENG-2410 (alert harmonization). No Jira tickets linked.

Notes on risk and mitigation: The quieting controller intentionally only targets a narrow set of cost/latency low-priority alerts initially. All muting events are recorded in a write-only audit log and surfaced on the dashboard. Ops can disable TFI-based quieting per-tenant with a feature flag.
